{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or below) to counteract over-optimism.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — model tends to overreact.",
    "When true outcomes show strong upward momentum (e.g., >70), reduce forecast peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.",
    "In periods with sustained negative sentiment, apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean to align with mean reversion.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, if history shows consistent downward drift, apply a slight upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.",
    "If sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., from -0.25 to 0.00), increase forecast sensitivity to recent price action by 10–15%.",
    "Avoid forecasting spikes in price when sentiment is neutral — model tends to overestimate volatility in flat periods."
  ]
}
